title: Cap. IX Sol: without simulation God can offer remission and life indiscriminately on condition of faith — reprobation decree is not 'even if Judas believes he will not be saved'
pass_a_gloss: These things having been first tasted, I answer that God without any simulation, such a decree of reprobation notwithstanding, can through evangelical ministers propose remission of sins and eternal life indiscriminately unto men under this condition, If they shall have believed in Christ. Nor does God simulate when under this condition he promises salvation promiscuously unto any men whatsoever, because unto any man fulfilling the condition he will faithfully exhibit the promised benefit. If the decree of reprobation were conceived in this form, Even if Judas shall have believed, he will not obtain remission of sins, or eternal life, there would be a manifest illusion as to the reprobate in the preaching of the Gospel. But that decree contains only this, I will not give unto Judas that special grace by means of which he would in fact fulfill the condition proposed. If they wish to convict God of simulation, they ought to show that God promised through evangelical ministers that he would give this special grace unto some person, whom nonetheless by an antecedent decree of reprobation he rejected from the same. If they shall have done this, which they will never be able to do, we (which God forbid) will suffer God to be prosecuted by them as guilty of simulation.
pass_b_english: With that premise I answer: reprobation decree notwithstanding, God can without any simulation, through evangelical ministers, set before men indiscriminately remission of sins and eternal life on this condition — If they believe in Christ. Nor does he simulate when under that condition he promises salvation to any whatsoever: to whoever fulfills the condition he will faithfully give the promised benefit. If the reprobation decree were cast as Even if Judas believes, he will not obtain remission or eternal life, Gospel preaching to the reprobate would be open illusion. But that decree holds only this: I will not give Judas that special grace by which he would in fact fulfill the proposed condition. To convict God of simulation they must show he promised through evangelical ministers to give that special grace to someone whom he nonetheless rejected from it by antecedent reprobation. If they ever do that — which they never can — we will (God forbid) let them prosecute God as guilty of simulation.
source_text: Hisce praelibatis respondeo, Deum absque omni simulatione, non obstante tali decreto reprobationis, posse per evangelicos ministros remissionem peccatorum et vitam aeternam hominibus indiscriminatim proponere sub conditione hac, Si crediderint in Christum. Neque simulat Deus quando sub hac conditione promittit salutem promiscue quibusvis hominibus, quia cuivis homini conditionem implenti promissum beneficium fideliter exhibebit. Si reprobationis decretum in hanc formam conciperetur, Etiamsi Judas crediderit, non obtinebit remissionem peccatorum, aut vitam aeternam, esset manifesta illusio quoad reprobatos in praedicatione Evangelii. Sed illud decretum hoc tantum continet, Non dabo Judae specialem illam gratiam, qua mediante conditionem propositam de facto impleret. Si Deum simulationis velint coarguere, ostendere debent, Deum promisisse per ministros evangelicos se daturum hanc specialem gratiam alicui personae, quam nihilominus antecedaneo reprobationis decreto ab eadem rejecit. Hoc si fecerint, quod nunquam facere poterunt, nos (quod absit) Deum simulationis peragi ab illis reum patiemur.
